newsitem.title: USA: RESEARCH ALERT - Kellogg EPS estimates cut.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - Kellogg EPS estimates cut.

text.p: -- Goldman Sachs analyst Nomi Ghez said Friday she cut her earnings estimate for cereal giant Kellogg Co to $0.75 a share from $0.85 for the first quarter, and to $3.30 a share from $3.40 for 1997.

-- In the 1996 first quarter, Kellogg earned $0.99 a share. Kellogg has said it expects first quarter earnings to be down compared with a year ago, with a spokesman adding the decline could be "significant."
-- Kellogg has said it expects a low double-digit percentage increase in 1997 earnings compared with the $3.07 a share before charges it earned in 1996.
-- Earlier, it reported earnings for the fourth quarter of $0.78 a share, up from $0.77 last year, both before charges.
-- "To the naive eye, Kellogg looks like an improvement in the trend," Ghez said.
-- However, Kellogg's selling and administrative expenses were down about 15 percent in the fourth quarter, with most of the decline coming from marketing and promotion spending, analysts said.
-- "When you realize how the company got to that (rise in earnings) it doesn't sound too encouraging," Ghez said.
-- She added that the stock is attracting some interest from investors that are looking for well-known, large capitalization stocks that have lagged the overall gains in the stock market.
-- "I think that the downside (for Kellogg's stock) is limited in spite of the estimate reduction because the stock has been such a laggard," Ghez said.
